parts.text: Identify the products of the reaction between fumaric acid and an excess of hot, concentrated, acidified manganate(VII).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Fumaric acid can form addition and condensation polymers.
parts.text: Draw the repeat unit of the addition polymer poly(fumaric acid).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Draw the repeat unit of the polyester formed when fumaric acid reacts with ethane-1,2-diol, $(\text{CH}_2\text{OH})_2$.

The ester bond should be shown fully displayed.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why polyesters normally biodegrade more readily than polyalkenes.

parts.label: (c)
(d)
parts.text:
The enzyme fumarase catalyses the reaction of fumarate ions, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$, with water to form malate ions, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{O}_5^{2-}$.

$$\text{C}_4\text{H}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{O}_5^{2-}$$

Describe, with the aid of a suitably labelled diagram, how an enzyme such as fumarase can catalyse a reaction.
